extracted.intended_audience: Authors submitting manuscripts to American Meteorological Society (AMS) journals, including BAMS
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing, formatting, and submitting manuscripts to AMS journals (including BAMS), covering required components, formatting, figures, mathematics, references, submission steps, and publication charges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author disclosure and transfer of copyright
rubrics_metrics.description: When a manuscript is submitted, the author will be asked to confirm that the publication has not been previously published in any language and whether it is under consideration by another journal. Each manuscript must be accompanied by a statement transferring copyright from the authors (or other holder) to the American Meteorological Society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must promptly inform the chief editor if the manuscript is submitted elsewhere before disposition. The appropriate copyright transfer form is available on the AMS Web site; signed transfer by all authors is required (original, faxed, or scanned versions acceptable). Editorial action may be delayed until the form is received. Individual authors may provide separate signed forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript length (standard articles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscript length should be less than 7500 words (including appendixes but not references or figure captions) or about 26 double-spaced typed pages when submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If paper exceeds the limit, the author must request Chief Editor approval via a cover letter uploaded with the manuscript explaining justification and requesting an exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript length (Expedited Contributions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Expedited Contributions must be no more than 2500 words (approximately 9 double-spaced pages), including the manuscript body through appendices, but not abstract, figure caption list, or references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expedited Contributions over the length limit will be forwarded to the Chief Editor for final approval. Note: Expedited Contributions may not have more than 6 tables and figures/figure files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submission requirement and uploaded files
rubrics_metrics.description: All manuscripts must be submitted electronically via the AMS online submission system. Authors must upload manuscript and figure files and required forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload double-spaced manuscript file(s) (Word or TeX) with double-spaced caption list, double-spaced table files (if separate), single-spaced captioned peer-review figure files (if separate), and cover letter if used. The submission system will automatically create a PDF for peer review which the author must view and approve before submission to the chief editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript components and order
rubrics_metrics.description: Each manuscript should include, in order: Title page (title, name/affiliation of each author, dateline, current/additional affiliations, corresponding author address and e-mail), Abstract (beginning on page 2), Text, Acknowledgments, Appendix(ces), References, Figure captions, then Figures and Tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title, author names/affiliations and contact details should appear on the first page by themselves; abstract should begin on page 2. Figures and tables (including appendices) should be placed at the end of the manuscript file, after the figure captions list, rather than within the body.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise (≤250 words) abstract is required at the beginning of each article (and sometimes shorter contributions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should summarize conclusions and methods. First-person construction should not be used in the abstract, and references should be omitted because they are not available per se to abstracting services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text structure and section/subsection numbering
rubrics_metrics.description: The text should be divided into sections, each with a separate heading and numbered consecutively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section/subsection headings should be typed on a separate line using numbered style (e.g., 1. Introduction, a. Data, 1) RADIOSONDE, (i) Experiment 1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgments formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for author acknowledgments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Omit the word 'number' from grant or contract acknowledgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendices
rubrics_metrics.description: Auxiliary analyses or tables subordinate to the main theme should normally appear in an appendix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each appendix should have a title and appear after the Body Text and before References.

rubrics_metrics.name: References arrangement and citation style
rubrics_metrics.description: References should be arranged alphabetically without numbering; text citation should consist of the author's name and year (e.g., Rossby 1945 or Smith et al. 1990).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When there are two or more papers by the same author in the same year, add distinguishing suffixes (a, b, etc.). Full reference formatting rules (journal, book, chapter, conference formats) are provided; references must be complete and properly formatted to allow cross-reference linking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred sources for references
rubrics_metrics.description: References should be to peer-reviewed literature whenever possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical reports, conference proceedings, and other gray literature should be referenced only when no other source is available; provide an 'available at' address for reports and dissertations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure captions and reviewer-copy captioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Each figure must have an adequate caption; all captions should be listed together, double spaced, for typesetting. For reviewer copies, single-spaced captions must also be included directly on the figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must include single-spaced captions directly on the figures used for reviewer copies. The figure number will be typeset and should not be part of the illustration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustrations and tables placement and citation
rubrics_metrics.description: Each figure and table must be cited specifically in the text and numbered in numerical order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures and tables (including those in appendixes) should be placed at the end of the manuscript file after the figure captions list. All tables should have a double-spaced caption, and table text and headers should also be double spaced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure file preparation and acceptable formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures printed in the journal are placed on the typeset page as electronic image files; authors should supply electronic files of images originally created electronically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Print-quality original figure files must be in accepted formats listed on the AMS web site. Files should contain only a single figure and should not contain captions. Multiple-panel figures should be combined into a single electronic file when possible. Authors should strive to submit figures at the size they will appear. Use the Digital Expert software to detect issues (fonts not embedded, RGB vs CMYK, low resolution).

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure appearance for review (print-as)
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures must appear for review as they will in print.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you want figures printed in black and white, provide black-and-white figures for review. Figures that change or are reuploaded during review are acceptable; if source files are included and captioned in the system-built PDF, AMS will not ask to remove those captions later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure panel labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should label figure panels with lowercase lettering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer labeling in the upper-left corner within the figure panel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table formatting constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables must not contain any shading, color, or underlining.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To highlight information within a Table, use italics or boldface font. Tables must appear at the end of the manuscript file with captions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical formulas and display equations
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid built-up fractions and other complicated equation structures in text; put complicated expressions as display equations centered on their own line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Display equations are usually numbered consecutively to facilitate citation in text (equation number in parentheses set flush right).

rubrics_metrics.name: MathType and math production guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Because of AMS typesetting requirements, authors using Microsoft Word are asked to use MathType for display equations and to avoid MathType in running text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use MathType for display equations rather than keyboard entries; avoid MathType in running text, using keyboard exclusively except for overbarred variables or stacked super/subscripts that cannot be created from the keyboard. This reduces production time for mathematics-heavy papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typeface conventions for mathematical variables
rubrics_metrics.description: Use correct typeface for variables: scalar variables set as italic (except multi-character variables), vectors as boldface roman, matrices/tensors as boldface sans serif; parameters used as subscripts/superscripts are italic unless an acronym/abbreviation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: scalar italic; e.g., V as boldface roman for vector; matrices/tensors boldface sans serif (A); subscripts like Tυ, TLCL, Vg, Vobs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Units formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Units should be SI with a few approved non-SI meteorological/oceanographic units; units should be set in roman font using exponents rather than the solidus (/), and with a space between each unit in a compound set (e.g., m s-1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use m/s or ms-1; use m s-1. Use approved exceptions only where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time and date formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Day, month, and year are written as '26 May 1998'. Recommended time zone annotation is universal time abbreviated UTC; time, time zone, day, month, and year are written as '1619 UTC 26 May 1998'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not abbreviate months except in figure captions or tables. Use 24-hour clock (astronomical/military time). Do not use Z or GMT in place of UTC. Other time zones (e.g., EST, EDT, PST, LST, LT) are permissible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting requirements for NEW submissions (typography and spacing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Text must be set using a 12 point font and double-spaced (3 typed lines per inch [2.5 cm] measured anywhere on the page), from the Abstract through Appendices. All pages must be numbered sequentially; line numbers are strongly advised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure and table formatting rules must be followed (figures/tables at end with captions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements to enter peer review (administrative checks)
rubrics_metrics.description: To be forwarded to the chief editor for peer review, a NEW submission must meet administrative requirements in addition to formatting requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements include: co-author verification from all authors (co-authors receive email and must verify), a completed/signed Page and Color Charge Estimation Worksheet committing to pay estimated page charges or applying for a waiver, and submission of manuscript and figure files. At submission the author must agree to pay estimated page charges or request a waiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-author verification process
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a corresponding author completes submission, co-authors will receive an email requesting verification; once they complete this step they are considered verified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signed copyright forms will eventually be needed for publication, but are not necessary for initial submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication charges and color fees, waivers
rubrics_metrics.description: AMS page charges are applied (e.g., $140 per printed page as of 1 Jan 2008); color figure reproduction incurs additional charges (varies depending on waiver status).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors estimate page charges using provided formula; payment is expected. Color charges example: $90 per figure piece if all page charges are paid; for partial waivers different per-piece rates apply (e.g., $490 first piece, $390 second, $150 additional). Authors with full waiver must convert color figures to black and white if possible. Inability to honor page charges will not prevent publication, but color charges generally must be paid; technical editor may assist to convert to black-and-white.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional requirements for REVISED submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Revised manuscripts must meet all requirements for new submissions plus additional items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revisions must include a figure captions list before individual figures and must supply manuscript and figure source files with all revisions. Figures must appear for review as they will in print; provide black-and-white versions if desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: System-generated PDF approval
rubrics_metrics.description: The manuscript submission system will automatically create for peer review a PDF containing the double-spaced manuscript, tables, and figures with captions below.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author must view and approve that PDF for submission to the chief editor.
